FINDINGS:

All five branches edit the same tracked file at the same insertion point: the newest changelog entry goes at the top of [CHANGELOG.md](/home/kesha/bench896/runs/A-R1-luna-r1/CHANGELOG.md). Because branches start from the same base, each insertion overlaps when merged in sequence. With five parallel branches, that creates up to four conflicts to resolve as later branches merge. Appending entries at the bottom would still make them collide at the shared end of the file.

The merge path is [`merge_worker`](/home/kesha/bench896/runs/A-R1-luna-r1/app/mcp_stdio.py:1229), which delegates merge work to [`merge_worktree_to_main`](/home/kesha/bench896/runs/A-R1-luna-r1/app/workspace.py:1111); it does not provide changelog-specific handling. There is no `.gitattributes` at the project root.

Cheapest durable fix: add a `.gitattributes` rule assigning `CHANGELOG.md` Git’s built-in `union` merge driver. For independent top-of-file additions, this should let Git combine both sides automatically, reducing these conflicts from up to N−1 to zero while leaving the agent’s changelog-edit workflow and tool-call count unchanged. The tradeoff is that union merging does not guarantee entry order; verify that acceptable for the changelog format.

Per-task changelog fragments would also avoid shared-file conflicts, but require changing where agents write and adding an aggregation step, so they cost more agent or orchestrator work per task.
